title: fix(app-shell): a record-scoped ConditionBuilder advertises the roots its host binds (objectui#9645)
body:
Fixes #9645

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`ConditionBuilder`'s raw CEL editor forwarded `scope` to `CelPredicateField` and nothing else, so its autocomplete offered whatever `introspectScope` advertises for that scope — every root ANY predicate site may see. objectui#8167 had already made the editor LINT at `record` on this mount; the suggestions never followed.

A mount that declares `scope="record"` now advertises `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS` (`record`, `previous`). A mount that binds more declares it through the new `roots` prop — the shape `ObjectFieldInspector` (`FIELD_RULE_ROOTS`, `FORMULA_ROOTS`) and `ConditionalFormattingEditor` (`ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS`) already use for their own surfaces. A mount that declares no `scope` forwards `undefined` and is unchanged.

**Suggestions only.** `roots` feeds `introspectCelScope`, which builds the autocomplete catalog; the lint hint is built without it. So the accept set is untouched: every spelling that linted clean before still lints clean, nothing the server does moves, and `HookConditionError` stays exactly as loud as objectstack#4775 made it.

## Both halves re-measured on this base, not taken from the card

| reading | instrument | answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what the editor advertised | `introspectScope('record').roots`, installed `@objectstack/formula` 17.4.0 | `record`, `previous`, `input`, `os`, `current_user`, `user`, `vars` |
| what the hook server binds | objectstack `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`, at `625db0e` | `ExpressionEngine.evaluate(expr, { record: record ?? {}, previous })`, then a thrown `HookConditionError` two lines later |

Both match the card: seven advertised, two bound. The defect is the size the card reported.

## The conflation this deliberately did NOT make

`ConditionBuilder` already carried a roots concept — `REFERENCE_ROOTS`, documented as the roots a value typed into the VALUE BOX may plainly reference rather than be quoted as literal text. **It is a different population and the two do not coincide**, which is measurable rather than a matter of taste: `REFERENCE_ROOTS` carries `org` and `parent`, and the engine's record scope advertises neither. Reusing it as the advertised list would have re-introduced the objectui#8155 `app` failure — advertising a root this editor's own linter refuses. Measured at this base:

```
org.id == 'o1'   -> ok=false  "bare reference `org` ... Write `record.org`."
record.status == 'done'  -> ok=true
```

The two lists stay separate, each with its own docblock saying which question it answers, and a case in the new suite reddens if anyone merges them.

## Why one declared default plus a prop, and not a single hardcoded list

`ConditionalFormattingEditor` could hardcode `ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS` because it IS the surface. `ConditionBuilder` is not: six mounts reach it, and their hosts bind different sets.

- the hook `condition` and the validation rule are evaluated on the SERVER, which binds `record` and `previous`;
- an action's `visible` / `disabled` is evaluated in the browser, where `useCondition` merges the row over app-shell's ambient predicate scope — `buildExpressionScope` publishes `current_user`, `user`, `ctx`, `os`, `features`.

Nothing a mount passes distinguishes the two, so the component cannot derive per-mount truth; declaring it is the mount's job, which is what the `roots` prop is for. The default is therefore the set every host binds, and the asymmetry decides the direction: over-advertising on a server-evaluated mount costs the author their write, while under-advertising costs a client mount an OFFER and never a spelling, because the accept set is untouched and the offer is restored by one declared prop. That cost is real and is listed under Acceptance notes rather than left to be discovered.

## Evidence

### Red before, green after

The pin fails with the forwarding removed and passes with it, run from the committed state, mutation and restore both proven on disk by `ablation-replace`:

```
mutate   roots={roots ?? (scope === 'record' ? RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS : undefined)}  ->  roots={roots}
         anchor 1 -> 0, blob 07a8aaa7b238 -> 0740055bd265   (on-disk, not an exit code)
red      vitest ConditionBuilder.mountRoots.test.tsx  -> exit 1
         5 failed: does not offer `os` / `current_user` / `user` / `vars` / `input` in a hook condition
restore  blob back to 07a8aaa7b238 == HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty
green    same command -> exit 0, 11 passed
```

The direction is worth stating precisely: only the five DOM absence cases flip. The derived pins and the two controls stay green under the ablation, because they read the advertised list and the engine rather than the forwarding — they fence a different drift and would redden on a different edit.

### Gates

All exit codes captured before any pipe. Everything except the full suite re-ran on the merged head `f65380b3`; the full app-shell suite ran at `3b811573`, and the merge that followed it touched `plugin-form` only.

| command | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.mountRoots.test.tsx` | 0 — 11 passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 30 test files naming `ConditionBuilder` / `ConditionWidget` / `CelPredicateField` | 0 — 335 passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` | 0 — 718 files, 7062 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` | 0 (after the closure build; its script runs `tsc --noEmit` AND `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is type-checked too) |
| `pnpm exec eslint` on the two changed files, `--format json` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` · `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` · `check-changeset-claims.mjs` | 0 · 0 · 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 — 0 new citations |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | 0 |

**The lint narrowing, declared.** The repo-wide population is `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint`), which is CI's run and was NOT taken here. Locally eslint ran over exactly the 2 files this diff touches (count read from the `--format json` output, not asserted). That narrowing excludes nothing: `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain.

`ConditionBuilder.tsx` ends with 0 errors and 3 warnings. One (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`) is at this base already. The two new ones are `react-refresh/only-export-components`, raised by exporting a constant from a component file — byte-for-byte the pair `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx` already carries for `ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS`, and `--max-warnings` is deliberately unset repo-wide, so they fail nothing. Said here rather than left for a reviewer to find.

## Acceptance notes

- **Consequence, in scope and deliberate:** the narrowing reaches every mount that declares `scope="record"`, because the component has one forwarding site. The client-evaluated mounts (an action's `visible` / `disabled`) stop being OFFERED `os` / `user` / `current_user`, which their host really does bind. They still lint clean when typed, and one `roots` declaration at that mount restores the offer — the escape hatch is pinned by a case in the new suite rather than promised. Worth a follow-up card; it is not this one's to land under the declared file surface.
- **Finding, filed as out of scope:** `CONTEXT_SUBJECTS` in this same file offers `org.id` as a row SUBJECT at every mount, and the record-scope lint hard-errors on it with the remedy `record.org` — the objectui#8155 `app` shape, in the subject dropdown rather than the autocomplete. `org` is not in `@objectstack/formula`'s `SCOPE_ROOTS` at all. It also offers `user.*`, which no server-evaluated mount binds. Both reach a different control than this card's, and repairing them changes what the row builder EMITS, so they are not folded in here. Dedup words: `ConditionBuilder CONTEXT_SUBJECTS` · `org root unbound` · `subject dropdown unbound root` · `SCOPE_ROOTS org`.
- **Neighbour checked, no collision:** `claude/issue-9464-admin-scope-invalid-draft` touches `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`, its test, `i18n.ts` and a changeset. It does not touch `ConditionBuilder.tsx`.
- **Scope fence held:** `ConditionBuilder.tsx`, one new sibling test beside it, one changeset. `HookDefaultInspector.tsx` is NOT edited — the trap closes through the record-scope default, which is why that default exists rather than a per-mount declaration at the hook mount.
